title: Symptoms Preceding Sports-Related Sudden Cardiac Death in Persons Aged 1-49 Years
authors: Stormholt ER, Svane J, Lynge TH, Tfelt-Hansen J
population: Review of symptoms before sports-related sudden cardiac death in persons aged 1 to 49 years
findings: Sports-related sudden cardiac death is a leading natural cause of death in young athletes (abstract).

In the background population, both cardiac and non-specific symptoms are often present before sudden cardiac death; both are present in up to 74% before sports-related sudden cardiac death (abstract).
The main symptoms are syncope, chest pain, palpitations and dizziness (abstract).
Knowledge of symptoms could potentially be used with non-invasive prediction models to prevent sports-related sudden cardiac death (abstract).
limitations: Narrative review of persons aged 1 to 49, so it does not cover older runners; the abstract gives no per-symptom frequencies. Screening by ECG is described as debated.
implications: Supports naming fainting or near-fainting, chest pain, a racing or irregular heartbeat and dizziness in the warning-signs list as signs to stop; no frequency or risk is quoted to the runner.

verification.notes: Crossref confirms title, journal, year, authors and DOI, with no correction notice; Europe PMC abstract (PMID 33409809) read on 2026-11-13 and each finding is stated in it. Task WS1.
